newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil sluggish, HSFO barges move at $91.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil sluggish, HSFO barges move at $91.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets were stable and quiet, with Monday morning sloth and summer doldrums combining to slow business, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $91 a tonne, in line with the higher end of business on Friday. Bunker demand was reported initially weak.

The expected arrival of large quantities of Russian fuel oil has not yet depressed prices. One regular buyer spoke last week of 120,000 tonnes of fuel oil loading in Klaipeda and St.Petersburg by August 4, and another saw 150,000 tonnes available by August 10.
The avails follow a period of scarcity in the Baltic which has taken E-4 straight-run premiums up to $7-$8 over the mean/mean/mean of published quotes.

Low sulphur straight-run is still attractive to refiners suffering from poor crude refining margins, with cargoes bought up well into the second half of August. Dealers pegged its value at $107/109 a tonne but one seller was heard offering 0.8 percent material for $109
One percent fuel was depressed by poor Mediterranean demand and business was sluggish, with values pegged around $94 a tonne.
